statement: DATO: Cheng 2020: ethosuximide lowered the PTZ-provoked stage in the knockout and was not significant in wild-type and heterozygous pups; wild-type stage about 1 on 0 to 6; no genotype-by-treatment test; the test age is not stated in the paper or its supplement.
depth: full text, held; figure read; supplement text searched
system_and_conditions: global Wwox-null mouse, preweaning, PTZ, ethosuximide pretreatment, 60-minute Racine stage

statement: INFERENZA: the SD of the 60-minute summary is a bracket, not a value; coefficient of variation of S about 0.6 to 1.2 in the knockout (within-animal correlation 0.6 to 1.0), the wild-type groups at the floor with coefficients above 1.4; independent reading by IT within about 20 percent (per-minute SD 1.15 against 1.32 in 7b, 1.53 against 1.26 in 7d).
depth: means and error bars of the figure; N assumed constant over the hour
system_and_conditions: Fig 7b and 7d, PTZ-alone knockout and wild-type groups

statement: INFERENZA: an interaction contrast needs twice, not four times, the simple-effect number per cell (4 (z sigma / delta)^2); with the bracket and wild type at the floor about 180 to 320 animals per cell, about 700 to 1,300 animals for one drug against vehicle; the genotype-by-treatment contrast is not attemptable with the full-hour summary at this variability.
DATO (abstract): rat PTZ ontogeny: ethosuximide effective only from about 25 days of age, not at 18 days or younger.
system_and_conditions: rat pups 7 to 90 days, PTZ, ethosuximide

statement: DATO: no mouse ethosuximide-against-PTZ ontogeny datum was found by two routes; one mouse pup datum for another seizure type goes the other way (SSADH-null pups P10 to P21, absence-like seizures abolished; abstract only, age of the drug test not stated). TRANSFER from the rat is unresolved.
depth: abstract; PubMed and Europe PMC queries
system_and_conditions: mouse pups P10 to P21, spontaneous GHB and GABA-B-driven seizures

statement: DATO: ethosuximide did not act on the low-threshold calcium current of rat and cat thalamic neurons in vitro (10 to 18 day slices) and reduced the persistent sodium current by about 60 percent; the T-type mechanism is contested.
system_and_conditions: rat and cat thalamic neurons in vitro

statement: DATO (search result, not biological absence): no WWOX-Cav3 link and no T-type current in any WWOX system by two routes; four held WWOX-deficient transcript sets disagree and none samples the thalamus or measures a current.
system_and_conditions: WWOX-deficient systems (bulk P17, P47T knock-in, organoids, snRNA by class)

statement: DATO (abstract): lithium lowered the PTZ stage in all three genotypes in the same experiment, so the pattern is the shape of a general effect.
depth: figure read; SCI exact values from the vector panel
system_and_conditions: global Wwox-null mouse, PTZ, lithium pretreatment

statement: DATO (abstract level, mostly rat): per candidate, valproate protects against PTZ at every age tested in the rat; ketamine acts on generalised seizures with ataxia more in younger animals; memantine and MK-801 raise minimal seizures; GluN2B-selective agents fade across the window; phenobarbital efficacious from P10 in the mouse; lithium and selective T-type blockers: no age-window paper found; diazepam is not age-flat in the rat.
status: supported at abstract level, blind-verified (11 of 12 claims, one partly)
depth: abstract level; about half one laboratory family

statement: WITHDRAWN: the statement that, in the mouse, high-dose diazepam or pentobarbital worsened induction at P11 and not at P14 and that bumetanide undid it (Kasahara 2019) is withdrawn as evidence after full-text reading by SCI and by IT: incidence of clonic seizures not raised, latency effect not blocked by bumetanide, all high-dose diazepam mice dead at P11 and P14, groups of 4 to 5, 17 of 29 recorded mice died, sedation and heat dissipation open.
depth: full text read by SCI and IT
system_and_conditions: mouse pups P11 and P14, hyperthermia-induced seizures

statement: DATO (label): ethosuximide safety and effectiveness are not established below 3 years; warnings include blood dyscrasias and immune-mediated reactions; no primary paediatric safety paper found.

DATO (abstract): selective-blocker genetics exist in another assay (a Cav3.1 and Cav3.2 knockout design with a selective blocker in a maximal-electroshock assay); no pup datum for selective T-type blockers was found by two routes.

DATO: Cheng 2020: lithium lowered the PTZ stage in all three genotypes; exact values from the vector panel: mean stage over minutes 1 to 60, +/+ 0.27 against 0.12 (N 12 and 8), +/- 0.42 against 0.16 (12 and 12), -/- 1.20 against 0.22 (6 and 7).
system_and_conditions: global Wwox-null mouse, PTZ, lithium pretreatment

statement: DATO: the only GSK-3 measurement in a Wwox-null animal is one p-Ser9 blot (one lane per genotype and region; the age stated as day 14 in Methods and day 20 in the legend); no kinase activity, beta-catenin or Wnt readout in Wwox-null tissue.
depth: full text; PubMed and Europe PMC queries

statement: DATO (abstract level): lithium in wild-type rodent PTZ and other models: acute raises the clonic threshold in several mouse abstracts; one family found acute pro-convulsant and chronic threshold-raising; the effect is very weak or absent in rats; potentiation of pilocarpine-type seizures several-fold; no lithium age-window provoked-seizure paper was found by two routes.

DATO (abstract level): other GSK-3 inhibitors: anticonvulsant in several provoked models, worse or opposite in others (status epilepticus worsened in one study; higher GSK-3 activity slowed kainate epileptogenesis in another); none in a Wwox model; tideglusib has no seizure-model result.

DATO (label and abstract level): lithium paediatric label from age 7 (bipolar), not established below 7 years; toxicity close to therapeutic concentrations; infant data are breast-milk exposure case reports only.

DATO (abstract level): GSK-3 inhibition and myelination: raised oligodendrocyte differentiation in some studies and suppressed it in others; conditional beta-catenin activation delayed developmental myelination; the sign is stage-dependent.
system_and_conditions: postnatal mouse, optic nerve, preterm rabbit model

statement: INFERENZA: the p-Ser9 fall (more active GSK-3, lower beta-catenin) and Dvl release (higher Wnt output) predict opposite beta-catenin signs in Wwox loss; neither is measured in Wwox-null brain.

INFERENZA: with a within-animal correlation of 0.6 to 1.0 the knockout PTZ-alone variability needs about 36 to 109 animals per arm for a ratio of 0.7 and an interaction about 180 to 320 per cell; the interaction is exploratory unless the pilot finds a lower-variability summary.
WITHDRAWN: any statement that a bumetanide-sensitive GABAergic aggravation in the mouse (Kasahara 2019) bears on the lithium or GSK-3 thread: withdrawn as evidence (see INV-04 D10).
depth: full text read by SCI and IT
